title: M3 §1–2 — opening discovery and why the CCB surface cannot be ported as a plugin: write the corrected finding, then make its load-bearing invariants executable
wave: Context (pre-wave) — runs before Sóng 1. S1–S6 all cite this item's claims as their premise, so its anchor drift is silently inherited by every downstream spec.
one_line: Before any M3 code is written, replace the plan's §1–2 argument with a finding doc whose every line number was re-verified against this tree, and add two tests that make the two 'the plugin surface is closed' claims fail loudly if a future contributor quietly opens a half-seam.
user_visible_effect: none — internal. The doc is engineering reference; the tests assert existing behavior and change no rendered output. The user-visible payoff is indirect and lands in S1 onward: because the closure is now pinned, an M3 engineer who tries the plugin route and gets a confusing half-working result hits a named red test naming the closed catalog instead of losing a day to a dead end.

steps.instruction: Do nothing else until this is read: the plan's §1–2 anchors are 6-for-11 stale. The correct numbers, all re-verified at HEAD 808b365, are: toolRenderers record at packages/tui/src/tools/index.ts:35 (plan correct); the `./*` subpath export at packages/tui/package.json:94-96 (plan says 93-96, correct to within the closing brace of the preceding entry); STATUS_LINE_SEGMENT_IDS opens at packages/tui/src/status-line/schema.ts:2 and closes `] as const;` at :30 — NOT 1-32; CUSTOM_STATUS_LINE_DEFAULTS at schema.ts:36-42 (plan correct); the seven presets at packages/tui/src/status-line/presets.ts:5,16,26,36,59,84,96 (plan exactly correct, all seven); setFooter/setHeader no-ops at packages/coding-agent/src/modes/controllers/extension-ui-controller.ts:157 and :158 — NOT 148-149, off by nine; #handleServerRequest at packages/coding-agent/src/mcp/manager.ts:1032 with the -32601 throw at :1039 (plan correct); `capabilities:` at packages/coding-agent/src/mcp/client.ts:101 with `roots: { listChanged: false }` at :102 — NOT 100-104; the type-only pi-tui import at packages/coding-agent/src/mcp/manager.ts:46 (plan correct); elicitFormFromAcpClient at packages/coding-agent/src/modes/acp/acp-agent.ts:314 (plan correct); setFrameProvider at packages/tui/src/tui.ts:949 (plan correct); the single non-test call site at packages/tui/src/prompt/composer.ts:302 — NOT 301, off by one.

Write docs/plugin-surface-closure.md. Structure it as four sections, in this order. (1) Goal and exclusions: port CCB's UX *behaviors* — scroll speed measurement, notification buffer with supersession, auto-display key hints, quota status band, MCP elicitation forms, overlay scroll chrome, colorblind-safe theme — while NOT forking packages/tui, NOT porting @anthropic/ink, NOT porting a React reconciler, NOT porting an alt-screen state machine, NOT porting CCB's dialog framework, and NOT porting mouse text selection. These six exclusions are decision-level, not deferrals. (2) The three opening discoveries, each with its verified anchor. (3) The three reasons plugin-porting fails, each with its verified anchor. (4) A short 'what this does not prove' section — see step 6, this is the section the plan's §2.4 argues for and it must survive into the doc.

In section (2) of the doc, record discovery 1 precisely, and correct the plan's mechanism. The plan says toolRenderers 'survives thanks to the export map ./* -> ./src/*.ts at package.json:93-96 PLUS a loader remap to the host instance.' Half of that is right and half is not. The `./*` subpath export is real (package.json:94-96) and it is load-bearing. But there is NO bespoke pi-tui remap in the extension loader. What exists is installLegacyPiSpecifierShim() at packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/plugins/legacy-pi-compat.ts:2727, installed at extensions/loader.ts:59, whose filter is LEGACY_PI_SPECIFIER_FILTER at legacy-pi-compat.ts:837 — a generic legacy-`@oh-my-pi/*` specifier shim plus a TypeBox shim (:873), not a pi-tui path remap. The actual reason a plugin shares the host's toolRenderers object is mundane and worth stating: the subpath export resolves `@oh-my-pi/pi-tui/tools` to the same absolute file the host imports, and Bun caches modules by resolved path, so both callers get one module instance and therefore one mutable record. Write that. Do not write 'a loader remap made it work'.

In section (3) of the doc, write reason 1 (closed status catalogs) with the addition the plan omits — this is the single most important correction in this item. The plan argues the union at schema.ts:2-30 is frozen and the barrel has no register*. True, but incomplete: there is a SECOND closed catalog the plan never mentions, at packages/tui/src/status-line/segments.ts:919 — `export const SEGMENTS: Record<StatusLineSegmentId, StatusLineSegment>`, an exhaustively-typed record listing all 27 renderers. Because it is `Record<StatusLineSegmentId, ...>`, TypeScript itself forces the second edit: add an id to the union and the build breaks until a renderer exists. That is what makes the closure compiler-enforced rather than merely asserted, and it is a much stronger argument than the one the plan makes. Also record the third must-edit site the plan omits: packages/coding-agent/src/modes/settings.ts:280 and :287 register the settings pickers with `items: { values: STATUS_LINE_SEGMENT_IDS }`, so an extension cannot surface a new segment in the picker without editing coding-agent too. Three hand-maintained files, one of them enforced by the compiler.

Also record, in the same section, the one place the hand-maintenance leaks. packages/tui/src/status-line/segments.ts:957 reads `export const ALL_SEGMENT_IDS: StatusLineSegmentId[] = Object.keys(SEGMENTS) as StatusLineSegmentId[]` — an `as` cast, not a checked derivation. It flows to getSegmentGalleryInventory() at packages/coding-agent/src/cli/gallery-fixtures/segments.ts:19. So the union->registry direction is compiler-checked while the registry->id-list direction is asserted. That asymmetry is the seam a future contributor would exploit, and it is exactly what the new test in step 8 pins.

Write reason 2 (MCP request switch is closed) and reason 3 (one frame door + a written scroll invariant) into section (3), then write section (4) 'what this does not prove'. Reason 2: #handleServerRequest at manager.ts:1032 handles ping and roots/list and the default arm throws -32601 at :1039; client.ts:101-102 declares only `roots: { listChanged: false }`; manager.ts's single pi-tui reference is a type-only import at :46, so the class that must answer JSON-RPC has no UI access. Reason 3: setFrameProvider defined at tui.ts:949, exactly one non-test call site at composer.ts:302 — anything wanting to hook the render loop must go through Composer, and there is no bypass for a self-managing overlay. Section (4) must state the limits the plan's §2.4 argues for: the dossier never analyzed runtime compatibility between CCB's render engine and omp's plugin contract, and there is NO evidence anywhere for the 'cell buffer' or 'pre-styled ANSI' claims from the original brief. Do not extrapolate past the three anchors without opening the file.

Record the acp-agent correction in section (3), because it is a claim a future engineer will otherwise act on. The dossier called packages/coding-agent/src/modes/acp/acp-agent.ts:295-410 'a working implementation of exactly this on the same form layer' and two critique rounds rejected it. That rejection is correct and the plan is right to keep it. State the direction explicitly: elicitFormFromAcpClient opens at acp-agent.ts:314, takes an already-shaped schema, and calls connection.unstable_createElicitation() at :358 to ask a REMOTE editor. It is outbound-only and renders no local form. It is a good reference for lifecycle — abort, timeout, listener hygiene, accept/decline — and the schema->form half is new work.

Write packages/tui/test/status-line-segment-closure.test.ts. Import STATUS_LINE_SEGMENT_IDS and CUSTOM_STATUS_LINE_DEFAULTS from ../src/status-line/schema, and { SEGMENTS, ALL_SEGMENT_IDS, renderSegment } from ../src/status-line/segments. initTheme() in beforeAll, as status-line-cache-hit.test.ts does. Three tests: (1) exhaustiveness both directions — every id in the union is a key of SEGMENTS, and every key of SEGMENTS is in the union; report the offending id by name, because that is the whole point. (2) ALL_SEGMENT_IDS contains exactly the union's members, in the same order, which pins the `as` cast at segments.ts:957. (3) renderSegment on an id absent from SEGMENTS returns { content: "", visible: false } and does not throw — call it through a cast so the test exercises the real runtime hole a widened union would open, and document in a comment that the cast is the point.

In the same test file, add the test that names the user-visible consequence, so the closure failure mode is legible rather than abstract. Build a full SegmentContext — copy the shape from createGallerySegmentContext at packages/coding-agent/src/cli/gallery-fixtures/segments.ts:24, which is the deterministic full context already built for isolated previews, rather than hand-rolling one — then assert that a segment id which renders nothing is DROPPED from the assembled bar, not rendered as a visible gap. This is the behavior at packages/tui/src/status-line/component.ts:2590 and :2603, where `if (rendered.visible && rendered.content)` skips it. The named contract: when someone widens the union and forgets the renderer, the segment silently vanishes from the status line and nothing warns. That is the failure this test exists to make loud.

Write packages/coding-agent/test/status-line-segment-picker.test.ts. Import cfgStatusLineLeftSegments and cfgStatusLineRightSegments from ../src/modes/settings, and STATUS_LINE_SEGMENT_IDS plus CUSTOM_STATUS_LINE_DEFAULTS from @oh-my-pi/pi-tui/status-line/schema (the coding-agent tests already use the package specifier, e.g. packages/coding-agent/src/modes/settings.ts:10). Assert (a) each register's `items.values` is the union — no id can reach the picker that the union does not name; (b) the registered default equals CUSTOM_STATUS_LINE_DEFAULTS.left / .right respectively, so the config default and the picker vocabulary cannot drift apart; (c) an id present in SEGMENTS but missing from the picker's values is reported by name. If the settings register's public shape makes `items.values` awkward to reach, assert through the resolved config entry rather than reaching into internals — the test defends the picker's vocabulary, not the register's field layout.

Do NOT write a test asserting that setFrameProvider has exactly one non-test call site. That is the banned source-grep shape under AGENTS.md: it reads an implementation file and asserts on its text, it breaks on a harmless refactor, and it passes while the behavior is broken. The plan ran `grep -rn "setFrameProvider" packages/ | grep -v "/test/"` as a research command and got 39 total / 37 in test — that is a finding to record in the doc, not a test to commit. Same for the barrel having no register* (a grep over a directory) and for the union having 27 members (a baked constant). Keep those three as prose in the doc; keep the two catalogs' agreement, the picker's vocabulary, and the silent-drop behavior as tests.

Do NOT assert in the new tests that CUSTOM_STATUS_LINE_DEFAULTS contains neither `status` nor `usage`. The plan states that as a present-tense fact and it is true today (verified: schema.ts:40-41 — left is vim/model/mode/path/git/pr, right is session_name/token_total/cost/context_pct, no status, no usage), but Sóng 1 item A1 is a candidate for turning `usage` on in the presets, and a test that hard-codes today's default is a landmine for the very work that follows. If a default-pinning test is wanted, it belongs in S1, written after the maintainer's P1 answer, asserting the answer rather than the status quo. This spec deliberately leaves it out.

Wire the doc into the wave specs by citing it, not by editing them. Each of S1–S6 should be able to replace a plan line reference with docs/plugin-surface-closure.md. Confirm at the end that the doc contains a single 'verified at' line naming HEAD 808b365 and today's date, so a reader six weeks from now knows the anchors were checked once and when, and knows to re-check rather than trust.

Run the verification. `bun run check:ts` must exit 0 — I ran it in this checkout at HEAD 808b365 and it passed, all sixteen packages reporting Done, formatting clean across 5445 files. `bun test` is BLOCKED and no amount of waiting will change it: the native addon is not built, so the runner reports 0 pass / 1 fail / 1 error with 'Failed to load pi_natives native addon for darwin-arm64' (I reproduced this on packages/tui/test/status-line-model.test.ts). Run the two new test files once the addon is built. Do not report ctx1 as done on check:ts alone — check:ts does not execute a single assertion, and this item's entire value is executable invariants.

test_contract:
Two files, one idea: the status-line segment surface is a CLOSED set, and the two new tests defend that closure at the three places a contributor would actually break it.

`packages/tui/test/status-line-segment-closure.test.ts` defends the union<->registry agreement. The two catalogs are maintained by hand in two files (schema.ts:2-30 and segments.ts:919) and until now nothing checked the seam between them; the only coupling is a `Record<StatusLineSegmentId, ...>` annotation that catches union-widening at compile time but nothing catches registry drift. The consumer-visible failure if it regresses: someone adds a segment id, the build stays green, and the segment SILENTLY DISAPPEARS from the status line — `renderSegment` returns `{ content: "", visible: false }` at segments.ts:950-953, and component.ts:2590 / :2603 drops it via `if (rendered.visible && rendered.content)` with no warning, no log, nothing. A user sees a status line that is quietly missing a field they configured. The third test pins ALL_SEGMENT_IDS against the union, closing the `as StatusLineSegmentId[]` cast at segments.ts:957 that currently makes the reverse direction unchecked and that flows into the gallery inventory at cli/gallery-fixtures/segments.ts:19.

`packages/coding-agent/test/status-line-segment-picker.test.ts` defends the third catalog, the one the plan never mentions: settings.ts:280 and :287 register the pickers with `items: { values: STATUS_LINE_SEGMENT_IDS }`, so the interactive settings UI can only ever present ids from the frozen union. The consumer-visible failure if it regresses: a segment that renders fine in the gallery can never be selected in the actual settings UI, and a maintainer adding one discovers this only by trying it manually. The default assertion catches the paired drift — the config default and the picker's vocabulary disagreeing means `statusLine.leftSegments` defaults to something the picker cannot show.

Deliberately NOT tested, and why: the 'exactly one non-test setFrameProvider call site' invariant, the 'the barrel has no register*' invariant, and the 'the union has 27 members' count are all real findings but each is the banned source-grep / baked-constant shape under AGENTS.md — they read an implementation file or a constant and assert on its text, they break on a harmless refactor, and they pass while behavior is broken. They belong in the doc as prose. Likewise the current contents of CUSTOM_STATUS_LINE_DEFAULTS are NOT asserted: Sóng 1's A1 may legitimately change them, and pinning today's default is a landmine for the work that follows.

gate:
All four legs green, and none of them is satisfied by check:ts alone.

(1) bun run check:ts exits 0 — verified in this checkout at HEAD 808b365.
(2) Both new test files pass once the addon is built. (2) is the leg that matters; without it this item is a doc with aspirations.
(3) docs/plugin-surface-closure.md exists and every line number in it was produced by a command in the verification block during THIS task, not copied from the plan. Spot-check that the six known-drifted anchors read 2-30 (not 1-32) for the union, 157/158 (not 148-149) for setFooter/setHeader, 302 (not 301) for the composer call site, 101-102 (not 100-104) for MCP capabilities, and 94-96 (not 93-96) for the subpath export.
(4) The doc's section (4) 'what this does not prove' survives intact — specifically that the dossier never analyzed CCB-engine/omp-plugin runtime compatibility and that NO evidence anywhere supports the 'cell buffer' or 'pre-styled ANSI' framing from the original brief. If a future editor deletes that section, they have re-imported the unverified claim this item exists to quarantine.

Do NOT add a test for the setFrameProvider single-call-site invariant. Its absence is part of the gate: if a grep-based test for it appears in the diff, the item is wrong, not merely incomplete.
gate_can_fail:
Yes, and leg (2) is the one that carries the item. The union<->registry test is a genuine two-source cross-check, not an echo: STATUS_LINE_SEGMENT_IDS and SEGMENTS are separately maintained literals in different files, so a regression in either — an id added to one and not the other, a registry key deleted, ALL_SEGMENT_IDS reordering — produces a concrete diff naming the offending id. The silent-drop test goes red the moment renderSegment's `if (!segment)` guard is removed or component.ts's `if (rendered.visible && rendered.content)` filter changes, which is precisely the moment a segment would start rendering as a visible gap instead of vanishing. The picker test goes red if a segment is added to SEGMENTS but not to the settings vocabulary — a real and likely mistake, since the two live in different packages.

The honest weakness: leg (3), the doc, cannot fail automatically. A stale line number in prose produces no red anywhere; the gate for it is a human re-running the verification block. That is inherent to a documentation deliverable and is why the executable legs were made to carry the invariants rather than the doc — the doc records the anchors, the tests carry the contracts.
depends_on: Nothing. This item has no upstream dependency and is the first thing that should be built — every S1–S6 spec cites its framing as premise, so doing it last is what turns one stale anchor into seven.

For leg (2) only: a built native addon. Out of scope for the engineer to fix; it is an environment prerequisite shared by every M3 spec. If it cannot be built, ctx1 stalls on leg (2) and that should be escalated rather than worked around.

effort: ~1 engineer-day. Roughly 0.5 day for docs/plugin-surface-closure.md — the verification commands are already enumerated in the verification block, so the work is transcribing verified output, not re-deriving. Roughly 0.5 day for the two test files, and that is generous: both follow existing conventions exactly (status-line-cache-hit.test.ts already imports renderSegment and builds a SegmentContext; createGallerySegmentContext at cli/gallery-fixtures/segments.ts:24 hands you a complete deterministic context instead of 40 lines of fixture). If the settings register's `items.values` turns out not to be reachable from outside the module, budget +0.25 day and assert through the resolved config entry instead — noted in step 10 rather than discovered at hour six.
risk:
The single most likely way to get this wrong is over-testing: reaching for a grep-based test of the 'exactly one non-test setFrameProvider call site' invariant, or a count assertion of 27 union members, because both feel like they are pinning the plan's argument. Both are the banned source-grep / baked-constant shape under AGENTS.md — they read an implementation file or a literal and assert on its text, they break on a harmless refactor (adding a second frame provider in S4 would turn a green suite red with no behavior change), and they pass while the actual behavior is broken. The plan itself ran that grep as a research command and recorded 39 total / 37 in test; I re-ran it and the count holds. It is a finding, not a test. Step 11 exists to stop this, and the gate names its absence as part of the contract.

The second-order risk is quieter and costs more: shipping the doc without the two catalogs' agreement test, because the doc 'proves' the closure by citation. If someone later adds a segment id and the build goes green, the closure claim this milestone was designed around is false and nothing catches it. The executable leg is the deliverable; the doc is the receipt.

plan_corrections.claim: The `toolRenderers` escape hatch survives thanks to the `./*` -> `./src/*.ts` export map at `packages/tui/package.json:93-96` **cộng với loader remap về instance của host** (plus a loader remap to the host instance).
plan_corrections.verdict: HALF WRONG — the mechanism is misattributed
plan_corrections.correction: The export map is real and is at package.json:94-96, not 93-96 (93 is the closing brace of the `./status-line` entry). But there is NO pi-tui remap in the extension loader, and the plan implies one. What exists is installLegacyPiSpecifierShim() at packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/plugins/legacy-pi-compat.ts:2727, installed at extensions/loader.ts:59, whose onResolve filter is LEGACY_PI_SPECIFIER_FILTER at legacy-pi-compat.ts:837 — a generic legacy `@oh-my-pi/*` specifier shim, alongside a TypeBox shim at :873 and bundled virtual/host namespaces. It has no pi-tui-specific branch. The real reason a plugin shares the host's `toolRenderers` object is ordinary module resolution: the subpath export maps `@oh-my-pi/pi-tui/tools` to the same absolute file the host imports, and Bun caches by resolved path, so both callers get one module instance and therefore one mutable record. State the true mechanism — an engineer who goes looking for the remap will not find it and may wrongly conclude the escape hatch is broken.
plan_corrections.evidence: `git grep -rn 'pi-tui' -- packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/` shows only ordinary type/value imports inside bundled custom commands (custom-tools/types.ts:21, custom-commands/bundled/annotate/*, etc.) and no remap hook. `git grep -n 'LEGACY_PI_SPECIFIER_FILTER' -- packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/plugins/legacy-pi-compat.ts` returns 837 (definition) and 2737 (use inside the plugin setup).

plan_corrections.claim: §2.1's whole argument: the union is frozen, the barrel has no `register*`, and `CUSTOM_STATUS_LINE_DEFAULTS` omits both `status` and `usage` — therefore a plugin must edit core to add a segment.
plan_corrections.verdict: CORRECT BUT INCOMPLETE — the strongest anchor is missing
plan_corrections.correction: All three sub-claims verify (barrel re-exports exactly component/metrics/presets/segments/separators/types and `git grep register` over the whole status-line directory returns nothing; CUSTOM_STATUS_LINE_DEFAULTS at schema.ts:36-42 is left=[vim,model,mode,path,git,pr], right=[session_name,token_total,cost,context_pct]). But the plan never mentions the second closed catalog, which is what actually makes the closure compiler-enforced: packages/tui/src/status-line/segments.ts:919 declares `export const SEGMENTS: Record<StatusLineSegmentId, StatusLineSegment>` listing all 27 renderers. Because the annotation is exhaustive, widening the union is a BUILD ERROR until a renderer exists — the compiler, not a convention, is the gate. A third must-edit site is also omitted: packages/coding-agent/src/modes/settings.ts:280 and :287 register the settings pickers with `items: { values: STATUS_LINE_SEGMENT_IDS }`, so an extension cannot surface a new segment in the UI without editing coding-agent as well. Three hand-maintained catalogs, not one; one of the three enforced by the type checker.
plan_corrections.evidence: `sed -n '915,947p' packages/tui/src/status-line/segments.ts` shows the Record with 27 keys in union order. `git grep -n 'STATUS_LINE_SEGMENT_IDS' -- packages/coding-agent/src/modes/settings.ts` returns 280 and 287. `git grep -rn register -- packages/tui/src/status-line/` returns nothing.

plan_corrections.verdict: UNSUPPORTED — the plan is right to reject it, and this is worth keeping verbatim
plan_corrections.correction: Verified: the dossier mentions `@anthropic/ink` and `React reconciler` only as scope exclusions and contains no cell-buffer or pre-styled-ANSI analysis. The plan's §2.4 refusal to extrapolate is correct and must survive into the doc verbatim. Note the one asymmetry that DOES have a real anchor and is not in the plan: segments.ts:957 derives ALL_SEGMENT_IDS from SEGMENTS via an `as StatusLineSegmentId[]` cast rather than a checked derivation, and it flows to getSegmentGalleryInventory() at packages/coding-agent/src/cli/gallery-fixtures/segments.ts:19 — so the union->registry direction is compiler-checked while the registry->id-list direction is asserted. That is the one real seam, and it is what the new test pins.
plan_corrections.evidence: `sed -n '955,957p' packages/tui/src/status-line/segments.ts` shows `export const ALL_SEGMENT_IDS: StatusLineSegmentId[] = Object.keys(SEGMENTS) as StatusLineSegmentId[];`. `git grep -n 'getSegmentGalleryInventory' -- packages/coding-agent/src/cli/gallery-fixtures/segments.ts` returns 19, returning `[...ALL_SEGMENT_IDS]`.
